bookmarks.text:
1) Small models can punch way above their weight

If you do RL the right way (RLVR / verifiable rewards), a smaller open model can close the gap with the giants on reasoning-style coding tasks.

bookmarks.author: Unknown
bookmarks.text:
2) Python is weirdly hard for models

Mixing languages in pretraining helps… until it doesn’t. Python’s dynamic typing can create negative transfer vs. statically typed languages. Meanwhile pairs like Java↔C# or JS↔TS have strong “synergy.”

bookmarks.author: Unknown
bookmarks.text:
3) “Coding scaling laws” aren’t uniform

Different languages require very different amounts of data to specialize well. Some “enterprise-y” languages look easier; Python/JS can be trickier (ironic, given they’re the most used).

bookmarks.author: Unknown
bookmarks.text:
4) MoE vs Dense = ability vs stability

MoE can be higher capacity, but it’s also more fragile during SFT. Hyperparams matter more, and routing stability becomes a real issue.

bookmarks.author: Unknown
bookmarks.text:
5) Code models are insecure by default

Train on public repos → you inherit a decade of insecure patterns. “Safety” fine-tuning doesn’t magically fix code security.

bookmarks.author: Unknown
bookmarks.text:
6) Structure > perfect facts for reasoning training

When you teach chain-of-thought, the model learns the template (how to break problems down) more than the literal correctness of every intermediate step.

bookmarks.author: Unknown
bookmarks.text:
7) “Lost in the middle” is still a thing

Huge context windows don’t guarantee huge context usefulness—important stuff buried in the middle still gets missed.

bookmarks.author: Unknown
bookmarks.text:
8) Multi-agent debate can cut hallucinations (if you set it up right)

Done well, it improves complex engineering outcomes. Done poorly, agents just reinforce each other’s mistakes.

bookmarks.author: Unknown
bookmarks.text:
9) The “alignment tax” on code is real

Safety alignment can reduce coding capability—and the paper discusses ways to reduce that tradeoff.
